scenes.text: Where are astronauts your closest human neighbors?
The loneliest place on Earth is often thought to be a scorching desert.
Instead, it sits in the South Pacific Ocean at remote Point Nemo.
The three nearest landmasses are roughly 1,670 miles away to the north, northeast, and south.
This makes it the farthest point from land anywhere on Earth.
No regular shipping or flight routes operate within 250 miles of here.
When the International Space Station passes overhead, those astronauts are sometimes your closest humans.
This extreme isolation also turns the region into an oceanic spacecraft cemetery.
Hundreds of decommissioned satellites have been steered directly into these deep waters.
Even the International Space Station is planned to crash here in 2031.
